name: Silkworm Larvae (Eri Polu)
instructions: 1. Thoroughly clean the silkworm pupae and boil them in water with a pinch of salt until tender.
2. Heat mustard oil in a pan until it reaches a smoking point.
3. Add chopped onions, green chilies, and ginger-garlic paste, sautéing until golden brown.
4. Add the boiled pupae to the pan and sprinkle turmeric powder and salt.
5. Stir-fry on medium heat until the pupae turn slightly crispy and brown.
6. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot as a side dish or snack.
description: Eri Polu is a traditional delicacy among the indigenous communities of Assam, particularly the Bodo and Mising tribes. It is prepared from the pupae of the Eri silkworm (Samia cynthia ricini) after the silk has been extracted. It is highly prized for its unique, earthy, nutty flavor and its high protein content, reflecting the sustainable, zero-waste culinary practices of the region.
